title: RBNZ Conway: inflation breadth and rate-hike rationale — reported headline
facts: Newsquawk's October 16 headline attributes to RBNZ Chief Economist Paul Conway reasonable confidence that inflation has not become broad-based, alongside the view that rate increases help contain energy-shock spillovers. The provider identifies its feed headline at 08:53 UTC and public-page publication at 09:13 UTC. The original delivery/interview time and a complete official transcript have not been independently verified.
interpretation: For an NZDCHF short this is two-sided: limited inflation breadth supports patience, but the stated case for hikes prevents assuming the RBNZ has turned dovish. Separately corroborated October 15 reporting kept October hold versus 25 bp hike open while retaining an upward rate bias. CPI on October 22 and decision/guidance on October 28 are more decisive than treating these remarks as a committee commitment. Newly located evidence; not claimed to be a new announcement at research time.
time_note: Chart anchor: provider's reported headline clock, October 16 at 3:53 PM Jakarta; public page 4:13 PM Jakarta.
